builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SHADOWPREFILL: Keeping Your Next Model Warm for Per-Step Model Routing in Agentic LLM Serving
summary: Replaces cold model switches in per-step routed serving (where the KV cache is discarded on every switch and the new model must re-prefill up to ~63K-token contexts) by prefilling the session context on the unchosen model in idle capacity, with shadow KV spilled to host memory. It costs a serving-stack scheduler that harvests per-iteration SLO slack, host-memory KV spill, a 0.4% energy increase, and requires running at least two model instances concurrently, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for production-sized models. It can fail when shadow prefills are incomplete (forcing a cold switch anyway), when normal traffic leaves no idle capacity, or when the workload does not use per-step multi-model routing, in which case there is no switch penalty to amortize.
rationale: The technique presupposes a multi-model serving deployment with concurrent instances and SLO slack to harvest, which a single 24 GB GPU or API-only setup cannot host, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable now.
technique: Shadow prefill for per-step model routing

claims.statement: Replaces cold model switches in per-step routed serving (where the KV cache is discarded on every switch and the new model must re-prefill up to ~63K-token contexts) by prefilling the session context on the unchosen model in idle capacity, with shadow KV spilled to host memory. It costs a serving-stack scheduler that harvests per-iteration SLO slack, host-memory KV spill, a 0.4% energy increase, and requires running at least two model instances concurrently, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for production-sized models. It can fail when shadow prefills are incomplete (forcing a cold switch anyway), when normal traffic leaves no idle capacity, or when the workload does not use per-step multi-model routing, in which case there is no switch penalty to amortize.
Cuts switch-call latency by 8.5-21.4%, LLM-call latency by 3.7-17.7%, and routed token cost by 22.5-46.1% on agentic workloads with per-step model routing; energy per request rises by 0.4%.
